Developers can now install the 7th beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate, just one week after the 6th beta was released. Here are the details.

Apple releases 7th beta of macOS 27

Last Monday, Apple ended a three-week beta hiatus by releasing the 6th beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate, which redesigned the window control buttons commonly known as "traffic lights." The 6th beta of macOS 27 no longer uses flat red, yellow, and green circular buttons, and adds a Liquid Glass-like effect (which actually bears a fair resemblance to the old Aqua style) to the minimise, maximise, and close buttons.

Beyond that, the 6th beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate did not add any other user-facing features or improvements, suggesting that Apple may be using the final few betas to fix bugs and improve performance and security in preparation for the official release.

macOS 27 Golden Gate will introduce a brand-new Siri app, along with a redesigned Siri AI. The system also features a new AI-powered version of the Shortcuts app, allowing users to create shortcuts using natural language commands; it also includes a Safari extension builder that operates via prompt instructions.

In addition, macOS 27 Golden Gate will introduce new Golden Gate-themed wallpapers and screensavers, while restoring the fixed-radius rounded corners used for windows and apps. This change reverses the macOS 26 modification that adjusted the corner radius based on the content of each window or app's menu bar.

The build number for the 7th beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate is 26A5421a. We are closely examining this new beta and will report on the changes we've found later.

How to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

Here's how to install the 7th developer beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General ➝ Software Update
  • Click the "i" icon next to "Beta Updates"
  • From the dropdown menu in the top-right corner, select "macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta"
  • Click "Done"

Have you discovered any new features in today's macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Let us know in the comments section.
